audit_findings.title: The earnings anchor may be a full fiscal year stale
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; a computed $762 million (17.3%) anchor increase would raise the base value from $297.11 to approximately the $344.30 market price, while filed nine-month FY2026 net income increased $715 million (20%)
audit_findings.mechanism: A newer fiscal-year owner-earnings numerator would replace the $4,408 million anchor and could also alter the growth assumptions.
audit_findings.evidence: We have historically generated significant cash from operations, and we expect to continue to do so during fiscal 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: The record does not demonstrate that fiscal 2026 results or the 2026 10-K were available on September 4, 2026, so this is not yet a demonstrated stale-data error. It is nevertheless reasonably capable of changing the conclusion: the filed nine-month results show substantial earnings growth, and the base case needs only about a 17.3% anchor increase to reach the quoted price. Fiscal 2026 owner earnings and the effect of the announced $300 million to $340 million restructuring charge remain unknown.
audit_findings.action: Establish the filing and release chronology as of September 4, 2026; if fiscal 2026 results were available, calculate fiscal 2026 owner earnings under the identical methodology and rerun every scenario and the buy-below price.

audit_findings.title: Lending growth may consume capital omitted from owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2025 net loan originations of $724 million less $429 million of secured-facility borrowing equals $295 million, or 6.7% of the $4,408 million anchor; if recurring, the computed base-case effect is approximately $5.17 billion or $18.28 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Recurring equity-funded additions to notes receivable are a maintenance or growth-capital cash requirement omitted from owner earnings when only property and software capital expenditures are deducted.
audit_findings.evidence: During the same period, we used $2.8 billion for the repurchase of shares of our common stock under our stock repurchase programs, $1.2 billion for the payment of cash dividends, $1.2 billion for the net purchases of investments, $982 million for payments for employee taxes withheld upon vesting of restricted stock units, $724 million for net originations of notes receivable, $500 million for the repayment of debt, $184 million for a business acquisition, and $124 million for capital expenditures.
audit_findings.explanation: The cash commitment is demonstrated, although the recurring amount needed to support forecast revenue is not. Fiscal 2025 used $724 million for net loan originations while secured borrowing supplied $429 million, leaving $295 million funded from equity cash. Fiscal 2026 lending also expanded, with $4.930 billion of purchases, $1.389 billion of sales, $3.125 billion of repayments, and $186 million of additional secured borrowing during the first nine months. A recurring deduction near the FY2025 amount would materially reduce estimated value.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile annual and trailing-twelve-month loan purchases, repayments, sales, charge-offs, allowances, and secured borrowing by product; determine the normalized equity-funded investment required for the forecast lending revenue and rerun owner earnings and all scenarios with that deduction.

audit_findings.title: The cash addition must exclude customer-restricted funds
audit_findings.magnitude: $0 misclassification demonstrated: $4,681 million cash plus $2,099 million investments equals the $6,780 million bridge, while $7,760 million of customer funds is separately reported with an equal $7,760 million customer liability
audit_findings.mechanism: Restricted customer funds would overstate the equity bridge dollar for dollar if included, but the filed components show they were excluded.
audit_findings.evidence: Funds receivable and amounts held for customers represent funds receivable from third-party payment processors for customer transactions, funds in transit to our customers, and funds held on behalf of our customers that are invested in cash and cash equivalents and investment-grade available-for-sale debt securities, restricted for use solely for the purpose of satisfying amounts we owe on behalf of our customers.
audit_findings.explanation: The April 2026 filing resolves this concern. The bridge exactly matches unrestricted balance-sheet cash and investments, which the filing states were not restricted. Customer-restricted funds appear in a separate $7,760 million asset account matched by a $7,760 million liability. Consequently, none of those customer funds entered the valuation bridge.
audit_findings.action: Retain the component-level reconciliation showing $4,681 million plus $2,099 million equals $6,780 million; no valuation rerun is needed for this finding.

audit_findings.title: Acquired-intangible amortization may conceal replacement spending
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; the FY2025 add-back subject to review was $637 million, equal to 14.5% of the owner-earnings anchor, and nine-month FY2026 amortization was $495 million
audit_findings.mechanism: Adding back acquired-intangible amortization increases owner earnings, while any recurring acquisition or equivalent replacement expenditure occurs outside reported property and software capital expenditures.
audit_findings.evidence: Our acquisitions have resulted in significant expenses, including amortization and impairment of acquired technology and other acquired intangible assets, and impairment of goodwill.
audit_findings.explanation: No supplied evidence establishes that the acquired customer relationships, technology, or brands require recurring replacement acquisitions. Intuit retained $2.928 billion of FY2025 research and development and $5.035 billion of selling and marketing expense, which may already fund substantial maintenance. Nevertheless, the add-back is large enough that an undisclosed maintenance component could affect value materially; the necessary component cannot be quantified from the record.
audit_findings.action: Break the amortization add-back down by acquired asset and acquisition cohort; compare historical acquisitions and other replacement spending with attrition, product obsolescence, and revenue retention, then rerun owner earnings using only the portion demonstrably non-maintenance.

audit_findings.title: The post-April share-event check remains open
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; filed outstanding shares declined by 0.731 million from 274.268 million on April 30 to 273.537 million on May 14, only 0.27% of the 282.635 million valuation denominator, but later changes are not supplied
audit_findings.mechanism: Share issuances or award vesting increase the denominator and reduce value per share, while repurchases reduce the denominator and increase value per share; a split also requires synchronization with the quoted price.
audit_findings.evidence: The number of shares (in thousands) of Intuit voting common stock outstanding as of August 26, 2025 was 278,805 .
audit_findings.explanation: The observed change through May 14 is not material by itself, and the valuation denominator exceeds May 14 basic shares by 9.098 million, apparently allowing for dilution. However, the record does not cover May 15 through September 4 despite an additional $8 billion repurchase authorization and possible equity-award activity. The direction and scale of actual post-May changes therefore remain unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Obtain filings and share records through September 4, 2026; reconcile basic shares, repurchases, issuances, vested and unvested awards, options, and any split, then recompute the fully diluted valuation-date denominator and rerun per-share values.

audit_findings.title: Unquantified legal claims could sit ahead of common equity
audit_findings.mechanism: An unaccrued settlement, judgment, defense cost, or recurring compliance expense would reduce owner earnings or require a direct deduction in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: In view of the complexity and ongoing and uncertain nature of the outstanding proceedings and inquiries, at this time, we are unable to estimate a reasonably possible financial loss or range of financial loss that we may incur to resolve or settle the remaining matters.
audit_findings.explanation: This is an existing contingency rather than a generic future risk, but no amount can be established. The latest supplied filing reports that the Fifth Circuit vacated the FTC order, which contained no monetary penalty, and that legal fees to date were not material. It also leaves the Ontario action and remanded FTC matter unresolved and states that a reasonably possible loss cannot be estimated. The prior $141 million state settlement does not establish the scale of the remaining claims.
audit_findings.action: Review all filings, court decisions, docket developments, settlements, accruals, and compliance-cost disclosures through September 4, 2026; deduct any probable or reasonably estimable unrecorded claim and incorporate recurring compliance costs into normalized owner earnings.
